## Natural history notes

A tiny native epiphytic orchid that is nearly leafless at maturity, relying on its slender, green photosynthetic roots to produce energy. Jingle Bell Orchid grows attached to the bark of trees, particularly in humid hardwood hammocks, swamp margins, and other moist forests of southern Florida. It produces very small pale yellow flowers, typically from late summer into fall. Its common name comes from the clusters of reddish-brown seed capsules that hang from the plant after flowering and resemble miniature bells. The species also occurs in the Caribbean, Mexico, and Central America and is listed as threatened in Florida.
